item.content:encoded:
I particularly like the implication that he creates things, like the aurora, and they retroactively have always been there.
Most depictions of god-like beings present their works as being out of place or unusual, I suppose to emphasize how spectacular they are. Like Elsa's or Dr. Manhattan's crystal palaces.
There is something really appealing to me about a de facto deity who is naturalistic enough that you can't be sure if he did the thing or was just there when it happened.

Timer expired. Edits made as discussed below. Author may revert at anytime.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

So, a big effect of SCP-992 is that those who view him while he views any weather pattern start to see nonsensical weather. Who is to say that that nonsensical weather is not an instance of SCP-1746 every now and then. As such, I am proposing the following edits:

Changing this:

When SCP-992 is able to observe any weather pattern, the perception of humans viewing SCP-992 will be changed. These humans will observe unusual and nonsensical weather and meteorological activities. This effect will persist for 10-30 minutes after the affected persons have ceased viewing SCP-992. While affected, subjects will be unable to refer to themselves or others by name.

To this:

When SCP-992 is able to observe any weather pattern, the perception of humans viewing SCP-992 will be changed. These humans will observe unusual and nonsensical weather and meteorological activities. This effect will persist for 10-30 minutes after the affected persons have ceased viewing SCP-992. While affected, subjects will be unable to refer to themselves or others by name.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.content:encoded:
Thanks Roget, the old version really bothered me.

The new guy is alright, enough to cancel my downvote, but I wasn't really grabbed by the new version enough to upvote.

The observations from the guy affected by 992's anomalous effect seemed to lose it's writing voice toward the end. The use of abbreviations makes the voice start off sounding like a good ol' boy, not too bright but not stupid either. When he starts describing the effects of the anomalous rain, however, he starts sounding philosophical. I suppose there might be some "bleed" from the anomaly, making him unable to explain the phenomena in a way that would be consistent with his usual vernacular, but it ended up sounding off to me.

If there were more examples of this anomalous weather, I might upvote. As is, he's just a guy that doesn't age and may or may not predict the weather.

item.content:encoded:
I can imagine the imagine the writing of this:

  1. Author wants to write an SCP that has a big effect on the world and is important
  2. Author decides that natural disasters are the way to go
  3. Author figures that some sort of nature man would be ideal for this
  4. Author inserts nature-type gaia man standard traits
  5. Author realizes that, when you write it up, causing/predicting natural disasters isn't as scary as they'd hoped
  6. Author expunges shit everywhere
  7. Author realizes that SCP has no impact if you expunge everything
  8. Author decides that bad things should happen if you make him angry
  9. Author hits the same problem as before when dealing with the bad things
  10. Author expunges again
  11. Author posts article

So yeah. An article should feel like a coherent story, not like a futile attempt to wrangle some tropes into the SCP format.

Very agree, Pig. Feels like half the article is redacted for arbitrary reasons. People who talk with him like him. The way the article is written, we're led to believe (even if the Foundation doesn't) that he's just a kindly wise man who predicts natural phenomena, not actually causing them himself. He's a textbook Magical Native and a bit of a Mary Sioux (thanks for the puns, TVtropes).

I'd love to see the article skewed more so that it was more implied that he might be causing the disasters, as a starter. Also, not having *everyone* find him wise and appealing would be a nice change. Removing some of the [redacted] as well. Personally I would just start over but a lot of people seem to like him, so he could be just fixed up.
